Incident Bot: [P1] Service: routing-gateway-us-east — elevated 502s and request timeouts for POST /v1/chat.stream — threshold breached at 07:40 UTC. Paging: Aisha (oncall).

Aisha (oncall): I'm taking the page. First look at metrics. 502s spiking, connection reset from upstream pools.

Tom S.: I'm online, can assist with routing plane. Any recent deploys in us-east?

Alerting Bot: deploy/route-proxy v3.4.1 rolled 06:55 UTC — no failures reported.

Aisha (oncall): Checking routing table: some backends showing 502s; backend id prefix: rgw-az1-*; health-checks flapping.

Nate (SRE): I'll jump into the LB and backend logs. Looks like nginx upstreams returning 502 with: 
```
recv() failed (104: Connection reset by peer)
```

Maya (CS): Queueing note: Customer ACME reported intermittent disconnected websockets ~07:42 UTC. Ticket #CS-4599. They saw partial responses then disconnect.

Aisha (oncall): Hypothesis: upstream runtime pods are crashing/restarting causing resets. Checking pod restarts and oom events. Running `kubectl get pods -n runtime-us-east -o wide -l service=chat-runtime` now.

Tom S.: I see frequent 1m restarts on runtime-az1 pods around 07:36-07:41. `kubectl describe` shows process exit code 134 (abort). Core logs show assertion in connection-handling code.

Nate (SRE): For mitigation: 1) remove az1 backends from load balancer, 2) scale up runtime pool in az2, 3) enable 429 throttling to reduce incoming tail-load. Applying step 1 now.

Infra Bot: LB update: removed 4 targets from rgw-az1 (change id lb-9921).

Aisha (oncall): Traffic rerouted — errors dropped to baseline within 3 mins. Good. We still need to identify root cause and whether rollback necessary.

Priya (PM): Confirming customer impact: Maya can you get list of affected customers and SLA exposure? We should prepare a public-facing note if any customer experienced >5min downtime.

Maya (CS): Early list attached in CS system: 3 customers reported WS disconnects, 1 reported partial output. No confirmed SLA breach currently; detailed counts incoming.

Tom S.: Investigating runtime logs: crash occurs in `connmgr.cpp:handle_stream` when handling multiplexed frames under high concurrent websocket connections — looks like a use-after-free in a connection pooling refcount path after the route-proxy started reusing connections aggressively in v3.4.1.

Aisha (oncall): Noted. That suggests a code regression in route-proxy could trigger upstream failure during connection reuse. Can we rollback route-proxy to v3.4.0 in az1 as test?

Nate (SRE): We didn't see the issue in other AZs but we removed az1 targets; to confirm, I'll roll back route-proxy in a test node in az1 to v3.4.0 and run a quick replay of traffic.

Infra Bot: deploy/route-proxy rollback to v3.4.0 started on test instance (id tnode-23).

Tom S.: Replayed synthetic websocket stress against test node. No crash observed on v3.4.0; reproduces on v3.4.1. Logs show reference count decrement in close path not synchronized.

Priya (PM): Ok we have plausible root cause: regression in route-proxy v3.4.1 connection reuse that surfaced under spike of long-lived websocket connections.

Aisha (oncall): Action before we escalate: 1) keep az1 out of rotation until fix/rollback across production, 2) schedule emergency rollback of route-proxy in us-east if canary validated, 3) prepare customer comms.

Maya (CS): I'll draft an interim message: "We're investigating intermittent disconnects affecting websockets in us-east; mitigation in place and full postmortem to follow." Shall I send now?

Priya (PM): Send an initial CS note; flag to update after postmortem. CC legal if any SLA exposure confirmed.

Maya (CS): Sent to impacted customers at 08:05 UTC.

Nate (SRE): Canary rollback completed for route-proxy to v3.4.0 in us-east canaries. Monitoring 5m — no regression observed. Proceeding with gradual rollback to the rest of us-east.

Infra Bot: rolling update: route-proxy -> v3.4.0 in us-east (change id roll-4412).

Aisha (oncall): After rollback completes, confirm LB health checks are green and drain az1 targets back.

Infra Bot: route-proxy rollback completed at 08:42 UTC. LB targets re-added to az1.

Aisha (oncall): Observed stable behavior after rollback. Closing incident as mitigated. Incident Bot: mark P1 mitigated?

Incident Bot: Incident incident-1767000456 status: mitigated at 08:45 UTC. Postmortem needed.

Priya (PM): Scheduling: propose 90-min postmortem 2 business days from now at 16:00 UTC to allow engineering to gather artifacts and reproduce patch. Who's required: Tom, Nate, Aisha, Maya, Infra owner, and a Tech Lead from route-proxy.

Tom S.: I'll prepare minimal repro and stack traces. Also will draft the RCA timeline.

Nate (SRE): I'll add infra metrics, LB logs, and canary telemetry to the doc.

Aisha (oncall): I'll capture the on-call timeline and handoff notes; note that during incident there was a 1m overlap where I handed to Nate while responding to another page — we should put that in the timeline as a handoff.

Priya (PM): Good point — include on-call handoff. We'll review whether pager load impacted response time.

Maya (CS): I'll compile customer impact: affected sessions count, customers notified, and copy of the sent interim message.

Priya (PM): Drafting action items now. Tentative list: 
- [R1] Rollback policy: enforce canary rollback automation for route-proxy (owner: Tom S.)
- [R2] Add a memory & refcount sanitizer job in CI for route-proxy builds (owner: Route-proxy TL)
- [R3] Improve websocket health-checks to detect connection reuse failures earlier (owner: Nate)
- [R4] Add an incident playbook step: during websocket service errors, temporarily prefer non-reuse connections (config toggle) (owner: Aisha)
- [R5] CS: prepare final customer-facing post-incident summary for review (owner: Maya)
- [R6] Post-incident follow-up: schedule patch release with tests and validate in canary for 48h before production (owner: Tom S.)

Tom S.: Will open GH issues for R1, R2, R6. Assigning reviewers and setting target milestone in 2 weeks.

Nate (SRE): For R3, I'll add an alert that triggers when upstream 5xx + connection reset spikes correlate with reused-connection counters > 0.5% for 2m.

Aisha (oncall): For R4, I'll add the playbook step and a safe-command snippet: 
```
kubectl set env deploy/route-proxy USE_CONN_REUSE=false -n gateway-us-east
```

Priya (PM): Next steps for RCA draft: Tom to create initial draft with timeline + root cause hypothesis by EOD today. Assign peer reviewers Nate and Aisha. After peer review, I'll do final sign-off and route to comms.

Maya (CS): I'll have the customer-impact numbers in the doc by 14:00 UTC tomorrow.

Priya (PM): Please include in the draft: exact timeline (alert, page, mitigation steps, rollback), contributing factors (code regression, insufficient canary detection, websocket health-check gaps), impact summary (number of customers, session drop counts, duration), and remediation plan with owners and due dates.

Aisha (oncall): Also include a note about the mid-incident handoff where I was flagged on another page; we should evaluate on-call load during multi-incident periods.

Tom S.: Draft link (placeholder): https://docs.internal/redwood/postmortems/1767000456-rca. I'll ping the channel when draft is ready.

Incident Bot: Reminder: tag incident with components route-proxy, routing-gateway, websocket.

Priya (PM): Assigning reviewers: Nate and Aisha. Review due in 24h after draft posted. Final sign-off: Priya.

Maya (CS): Noted. Adding CS approval flow to doc: CS review -> legal (if SLA exposure) -> customer comms.

Infra Bot: Incident-1767000456: actions recorded. Postmortem scheduled.

Tom S.: One more item: let's capture the exact git diff that introduced connection reuse change and include it in the RCA. I'll link the PR.

Aisha (oncall): Okay team, thanks for quick mitigation. If you add any logs or notes to the doc, mention timestamps and pod ids. Closing thread for now — will re-open if more is needed before the postmortem. :white_check_mark:"
